Be filled with God's love and bear the ninefold fruit of the Spirit toward each other (920 practice)
Time, money and intimacy: becoming good stewards together in everyday life
Speak the truth in love, learn to reconcile and forgive, and live out mutual submission

steps.m: The Holy Spirit is my guide

partnerQ.t: Spirit: Where did the Holy Spirit prompt or move me this week?
Insight: Which verse helped us understand God's heart for marriage this week?
Life: When did I live like Jesus this week? And when was the self on the throne?
Service: How will I serve you next week, so that Jesus reigns in our home?
Glory: What grace shall we thank God for together, giving the glory to Jesus?

examen.t: What grace did I see in my spouse today?
examen.h: Thanksgiving: even small things count — and you can tell them

examen.t: When was the self on the throne today?
examen.h: Repentance: pride, impatience, coldness or control?

examen.t: How can I let Jesus reign in our home tomorrow?

assess: We pray or read the Bible together.
We seek God's will together on important decisions.
I can admit my wrongs first without rushing to defend myself.
I am willing to lay down my preferences for my spouse's good.
I often show love in ways my spouse can feel.
My spouse knows I appreciate and thank them.
I can listen to my spouse to the end without interrupting or fixing.
I can say what I really need instead of blaming.
After an argument, we reconcile within a day or two.
In conflict, I can see my own part first.
I don't bring up old wrongs.
I have handed past hurts to God and chosen to forgive.
We respect each other; neither of us controls the other.
We consider each other's views when making decisions.
We have time set apart just for the two of us every week.
We can put our phones down and be fully present.
We are open with each other about money, with nothing hidden.
We decide our budget and giving together.
Our physical intimacy is mutually fulfilling and respectful.
We share our hearts and feel emotionally close.
Between my family of origin and my spouse, I know my spouse comes first.
We honor both sets of parents and keep healthy boundaries.
We have regular family worship or spiritual time.
We are willing to walk alongside and bless other couples or families.

mendSteps.t: When conflict escalates, stop. Say, “I need a short pause; let's talk properly in a little while.” Breathe, and tell the Lord, “Lord, you reign here right now — not me.”
mendSteps.q: What I want to say to the Lord right now

mendSteps.t: First take the log out of your own eye. Don't ask, “Where is my spouse wrong?” Ask, “Where is my self on the throne?” — pride, impatience, coldness, control, or wanting to win?
mendSteps.q: In this conflict, my part was…

mendSteps.t: Humility draws out humility. Own only your part — no “but”. Be specific, brief and sincere.
mendSteps.q: I will say: “I'm sorry. I was wrong to…”
mendSteps.ph: I'm sorry. I was wrong to…

mendSteps.t: Ask your spouse to forgive you, and hand what they owe you over to God. Forgiveness isn't pretending nothing happened; it is choosing not to collect the debt. (Forgiving never means staying in danger.)
mendSteps.q: What I want to ask forgiveness for / what I choose to forgive
mendSteps.ph: Will you forgive me? I also choose to…

mendSteps.t: Make reconciliation real with one concrete action. People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things.
mendSteps.q: Or write your own act of reconciliation

mendActs: Set a time to talk it through
Do one small act of service for them
Write a note of apology or thanks
META.prayConfess: Lord, I confess that in this matter I wanted to be king. My pride, impatience and coldness hurt my spouse and grieved you. Forgive me and cleanse me. Give me a humble heart to admit my wrong first and to seek peace first. In Jesus' name, Amen.
META.prayForgive: Lord, you have forgiven all my debt. I place what my spouse owes me into your hands; I will not collect it or keep bringing it up. Heal the hurt in my heart, give me wisdom and safety, and reconcile us again in you. In Jesus' name, Amen.
fightRules: Address the issue, not the person: say “I feel…”, not “You always…”
No bringing up the past; one issue at a time
No arguing in front of the children or others
Never say “divorce”, never threaten, never give the silent treatment
No hitting, no throwing things, no insults
If emotions run too high, pause — and agree on a time to come back
Don't let the sun go down on your anger: before sleep, at least say “I love you; let's talk tomorrow”
hotlines: Call your local emergency number or domestic-violence helpline
Get to a safe place first, then call the police

I18N.xzSystem: You are “Xiaozhi”, the AI marriage companion in the “321 Marriage Life” app of Kingdom 321 Fellowship. You are an evangelical, God-fearing pastor, Bible teacher and marriage-ministry coworker. Respond in the spirit of the 321 framework: three foundations (Jesus is my example, Scripture is my standard, the Holy Spirit is my guide), two cores (let Jesus reign, let Jesus receive all the glory) and one purpose (build God's order, beginning with a household that belongs to God). Help couples move from the old self-ruled life into the new self-emptied life, where humility overcomes pride and humility draws out humility. Be clear and simple, use analogies, be warm and hopeful, quote the World English Bible with references, answer in English, and keep it concise. Always guide the user to start from “how can I change?”; never help one spouse build a case against the other, and never decide for anyone whether to divorce. Safety: if the user mentions physical, verbal, sexual or financial abuse, threats, control, self-harm or wanting to hurt someone, first express care, state clearly that submission and forgiveness never require this, that safety comes first, and encourage them to contact local emergency services, a domestic-violence helpline, their pastor and professionals right away; never encourage staying in danger. You are not a counselor: for affairs, addictions or serious psychological distress, recommend seeking pastoral and professional help.

MAT 6:11.t: Give us today our daily bread.

MAT 6:12.t: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.

MAT 6:13.t: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
